text:
alex: Ran a long nsys trace on the 4-GPU cluster to investigate the weird tail latency from last night. attaching notes below.

maria: thanks — can you drop the command you used? :eyes:

alex: nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output=run1.nsys-rep --sample=cpu --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite 
(we bound it to one model shard and replayed a mixed seq-len workload)

jing: did you see the dispatch stalls we suspected (dispatcher waiting on kernel selection)?

alex: yup. timeline shows repeated gaps ~1.4ms between dispatch and kernel launch on GPU1. NVTX spans show: "batch_dispatch" -> delay -> "cudaLaunchKernel". I pasted the timeline snippet: 
```
TIMELINE: 14:03:21.112 batch_dispatch (thread 56)
TIMELINE: 14:03:21.113 wait_for_kernel_selection (gpu1) 1.38ms
TIMELINE: 14:03:21.114 cudaLaunchKernel my_gemm_kernel_q8 0.8ms
TIMELINE: 14:03:21.115 kernel_complete
```

sam: interesting — is kernel selection doing a fallback to a generic GEMM often? that can add overhead if we run the heuristics synchronously.

alex: That's the thing. Kernel selector decision logs show a pattern: when seq_len < 64 and batch_size between 3-6, the selector picks a quantized kernel normally, but occasionally it falls back to a safe fp16 gemm path because the tiling heuristic estimated high register pressure. Logged decisions: 
```
[2026-02-18T14:03:21Z] selector: preferred=q8_tile_v2 score=0.82
[2026-02-18T14:03:21Z] selector: safe_fallback=fp16_gemm reason=register_estimation_variance
```

maria: any correlation to KV cache hits? we've seen cold prefix churns increasing scheduler jitter.

alex: yes — KV stats from the same run: prefix_cache_hit_rate overall 68% but for short prefixes (<12 tokens) hit_rate ~43%. Hotspot: most requests with short prefixes caused the runtime to rehydrate KV then trigger kernel selection code path under lock. That lock + fallback path -> dispatch stall.

nsys-bot: summary: GPU1 average dispatch-latency 1.12ms (p95 2.9ms). Kernel selection CPU time 0.36ms average. KV rehydrate added up to 0.9ms in the worst-case samples.

jing: so two fronts: reduce KV rehydrate for short prefixes (micro-caching or fingerprinting) and make kernel selection non-blocking (speculative selection + background verification).

sam: agree. quick experiment idea: bypass selector for known-good seq_len/batch combos (cache the selection key) and set a stress flag to force fallback only if we hit runtime errors. basically optimistic selection.

alex: did an initial patch on my branch: selector now caches (model_id, seq_bin, batch_bin) -> kernel_choice with 10s TTL. Re-ran trace with that enabled: dispatch-latency avg dropped to 0.45ms and p95 0.9ms for the same workload.

maria: nice. any negative regressions in accuracy or stability?

alex: no correctness issues in 10k inferences. One anomaly: quantized kernel sometimes had slightly higher token latency variance when sequence tails had extreme sparsity — but no incorrect outputs.

jing: worth adding a quick fallback counter: if kernel_launch fails or timeouts, mark entry as bad and trigger re-eval.

sam: also consider adjusting batching heuristic: current policy aggregates batches up to 8 but we observed many batches of 3-4 where selector thrashes. Maybe increase min_batch_for_fast_path=6 for q8 kernels to reduce selector churn.

alex: noted. I'll open a PR with two toggles: cache-based optimistic selection + min_batch threshold. I'll attach the reduced nsys rep and a perfetto link.

maria: can you add a tiny perf counter dump? curious about SM utilization pre/post.

alex: pre-patch sample: SM util 46%, SM stalls 38%, mem_bandwidth 210 GB/s. post-patch: SM util 73%, SM stalls 12%, mem_bandwidth 255 GB/s. Gains mostly due to less idle time between dispatches.

nsys-bot: artifact: https://internal-perf/reports/2069991234/run1-reduced.nsys-rep (perm: eng-runtime)

jing: ok next steps: 1) PR with toggles + unit tests for selector cache TTL 2) add micro-cache for short prefixes (fingerprint->KV pointer) 3) canary on dedicated cluster 4) instrument per-route kernel-fallback counters for alerts

sam: +1. I can help with canary infra and alert rules.

maria: thanks Alex — this explains the p95 spikes last night. please tag eng-oncall when you start the canary. :thumbsup:
